target_customer: Consumers and professionals who needed to send very large files quickly to another person
problem: Sending large files meant email limits or slow uploads to a server and then downloads. Sendoid sent files peer to peer so the recipient could download directly.
business_model: Free consumer web and desktop app; no monetization described in sources

founders.name: John Egan
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. TechCrunch (March 2011) says his earlier prototype iSendr drew nearly 20,000 visitors on its first day.

founders.name: Zac Morris
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch in March 2011 described him as a former Apple engineer. The YC page says he worked in application security at Facebook and managed Uber's mobile security team, and says Sendoid was acquired by Facebook.

competitors.name: YouSendIt
competitors.what: Large file email and later cloud storage service
competitors.traction_then: established service, added Dropbox style storage in July 2011

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser based peer to peer transfer needed NAT traversal and a desktop app for large files, which made reliability hard; one reviewer found it did not work on most test machines.

defensibility.rationale: Many free alternatives existed and peer to peer transfer offered speed but no lock in. The product was copyable by well funded competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YouSendIt added Dropbox style cloud storage in July 2011. Sendoid itself was reportedly acquired by Facebook, per the YC profile of its co-founder, with no date or terms found.

market_need_then: Large attachments were a common pain in 2011 and TechCrunch cited the co-founder's claim of a 100MB transfer in about 35 seconds against 25 to 30 minutes on server based services. The earlier prototype iSendr drew nearly 20,000 visitors in a day.

branding.domain_note: Used sendoid.com, which now redirects to caffeinatedmind.com, the legal entity (Caffeinated Mind Inc) behind it.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as the last file transfer service you will need, per TechCrunch coverage

rebrands.why: iSendr was the earlier prototype name; the reason for the rename is not stated in sources opened

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch, Gizmodo and blogs; prototype drew about 20,000 visitors in one day; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Press at launch and a viral prototype, but no sourced evidence of lasting brand identity or community.

outcome_analysis: Sendoid built a fast peer to peer file sender that drew attention at launch in March 2011, but it faced crowded competition from Dropbox, YouSendIt and others with no moat. It was reportedly acquired by Facebook, which looks like a small team acquisition, though the date, price and any product continuation are not public in the sources found.
notes: The acquirer Facebook comes from the YC profile of Zac Morris; a WebProNews article (HTTP 403 on fetch, seen only in search results) also reports Facebook bought Caffeinated Mind, the developer of Sendoid. Acquisition date and price not found. TechCrunch says Sendoid was raising its first angel round in March 2011; no amount found so no round recorded. The acquihire_soft_landing factor is an inference from team size of two and is flagged as such. Education not found. Founder prior employer for Morris of Apple is from TechCrunch; Facebook and Uber are from the YC page and are later roles.
